text:
maya: Quick syncI'm drafting an 'admission gateway' checklist for model onboarding that adapts checks by SLA tier and model footprint. want quick feedback on which checks are mandatory vs advisory.
ben: +1. concrete example?
kai: classify by param/size buckets and select a smoke suite per bucket. avoids running full microbench for every intake.
sophia: emphasize deterministic signals for rollout. lightweight probes must map to canary metrics or they'll be noisy.
maya: proposed buckets: tiny (<1B), small (1-7B), medium (7-70B), large (70B+). defaults per bucket.
elena: where do we draw boundary between onboarding vs runtime responsibility? e.g. kv-cache semantics.
ben: basic kv sanity (prefix caching, no corruption) = onboarding. long-tail eviction under load = runtime.
kai: compatibility checks should cover tensor shapes, dtypes, attention-mask semantics. if a shim is used, record shim=true in metadata.
sophia: encode adaptivity as single config blob used by intake + gatekeeper. sample:```yaml
buckets:
  tiny:
    probes: [latency_smoke, safety_basic, decode_consistency]
    max_wall_time: 10m
  large:
    probes: [latency_smoke, full_microbench, eval_regressions]
    max_wall_time: 2h
policies:
  allow_shim: true
  ramp_to_dedicated_if_latency_ms_gt: 300
```
maya: tie max_wall_time to SLA tier: free -> short, enterprise -> allow longer benches.
elena: cost accounting: large-model microbenches are expensive. require approval or charge team credits.
ben: add preflight approval if estimated GPU-minutes > THRESH. integrate with approvals bot.
deploy-bot: estimate for model "llama2-78b-quant" = 420 GPU-minutes for full_microbench. approval required.
kai: failure modes: if heavy bench times out, allow graded admission? partial canary? or reject?
sophia: graded admission preferred. fail-open for non-security issues with low-qps canary + telemetry gating. fail-closed for safety or contract breaks.
maya: deterministic gates for full admission: compile_success, decode_consistency(<1% diff vs golden), safety_no_hits, basic_latency(<tier_target). others advisory.
elena: registry metadata must include: runtime_abi_version, quant_type, max_seq_len, kv_cache_semantics, shim_applied (true/false). helps runtime routing.
ben: onboarding should emit an admit_token with metadata + provenance (bench artifacts, git ref, run_id). runtime can refuse stale tokens.
kai: also store reproducibility hash: weights_hash + export_cfg + seed.
sophia: bench regressions over time: need temporal baselines and small golden input sets per bucket/domain. bench must report variance; if above threshold, flag.
maya: golden sets per (bucket, domain) and deterministic metrics. use synthetic + sanitized traces.
ben: golden inputs must avoid copyrighted content.
elena: rollout playbook: onboard -> canary (qps 1% for 24h) -> ramp 5/20/100% with automatic rollback on metric breach. metrics: p50/p95, error-rate, safety_hits, quality_delta_on_golden.
kai: realize canary throttle via routing tags from admit_token. runtime router weights on tags.
maya: offer "fast-entry" experimental path: minimal checks, tagged experimental with explicit warnings in registry.
sophia: label schema: admit.level = full|experimental|restricted and reasons list.
ben: infra note: microbench must run on both A100 and H100; label results by hw.
elena: security: checksum verification of artifacts, ephemeral creds for bench runs, audit logs for heavy-bench triggers.
kai: actions: 1) maya -> draft adaptive config schema (ETA Wed). 2) ben -> stub admit_token proto + examples. 3) sophia -> assemble golden sets. 4) elena -> prototype approval gating with deploy-bot.
maya: one more: integration test for shim detection; fail admission if shim unsupported in target runtime.
ben: sample admit_token example:```json
{"model":"llama2-70b","hash":"sha256:...","admit":{"level":"experimental","bucket":"large"},"benches":[{"name":"latency_smoke","result":"pass","hw":"A100","run_id":"r123"}]}
```
maya: thanks all. i'll draft RFC with schema and admit_token proto by wed EOD. :thumbsup:
